Koreans use three levels of communication; depending on your age as compared to the other and the environment where the conversation is taking place.

Formal, polite and informal.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

In South Korea, communication is often described through three broad levels of language and social formality. These levels are especially important in understanding Korean culture because the way people speak reflects age, social status, familiarity, and the nature of the relationship.

## Three levels of communication in Korean

[Business Partners Introductionary Handshake Bow \| Premium Photo - rawpixel](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/gO6uoGh_PAIATng9rTT1jUyegyYP15GW1PS4cw8K0qLj2rCdZhqu5Xk_RoeCjbz3Mxcg4Pm3QI6JjdqUZW8Muf_JDnb_HBB9PT2wW1GAWrXTT4x3fA5RRa40H0FDU1QpqGISPejB1k1ZEaOGP3sSPFNI9TfRa5PujtC036ZvxHw?purpose=inline)

1\. Formal / Honorific (존댓말 – Jondaetmal)

Used when speaking to elders, superiors, customers, strangers, and people deserving respect. Common in business settings, public interactions, and formal occasions.

-   Polite verb endings: `-습니다 / -ㅂ니다`

-   Respectful expressions and titles

-   Often accompanied by formal greetings and bowing

Example: 안녕하십니까? (How do you do?)

[Business people having meeting in cafe](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/-g258bcAnHnyh476wW7S5czzfbnuIbr8Fn-JW3q3nS7hNqwmFaL-ySFgzliJXgf3Jg2KF6yhHgce76QxN-ILW3GYvobp32UEjsdTfFOC6EV_2PdSKI_t5_4n7yGVNYciXZIFe70r5D0Db2Jl2FELzJ8TOauDx1VmOh-dZqBd2gJVRu-5I2A9pjP4SusXNYlz?purpose=inline)

2\. Polite Conversational (해요체 – Haeyoche)

Used in everyday interactions with people who are not intimate friends but with whom one wants to maintain courtesy. This is probably the most useful level for visitors and everyday social situations.

-   Polite verb ending: `-요`

-   Friendly but respectful

-   Common in shops, restaurants, and casual workplace conversations

Example: 안녕하세요? (Hello.)

[Fall campus lifestyle of female college students](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/WFR2x3_5YViV0k0HfgB1SPOW-R_S7o-28m3aN16moGzXX7vfrLK-IrZZHsGYXLLwuv6vA4F29M24Fo3rYwCCB_56nXG4O_6lcFgwvrlK1i28vEv672VVFtSAZyxOerbMJQ2AsnDKvSSnjqs4-xJ3xGPiqJqR8SVcyPz3DHxSNTWSvdA95iTgnAN9-HBYVHqD?purpose=inline)

3\. Informal / Intimate (반말 – Banmal)

Used among close friends, siblings, people of similar age who have established familiarity, and sometimes between older and younger people.

-   No polite `-요` ending

-   More direct and relaxed expressions

-   Can convey closeness, but can sound disrespectful if used inappropriately

Example: 안녕! (Hi!)
